newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-THOUSANDS GATHER IN DORTMUND FOR EUROPEAN CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-THOUSANDS GATHER IN DORTMUND FOR EUROPEAN CUP FINAL.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Borussia Dortmund fans clad in the club colours of yellow and black packed into the centre of the German city on Wednesday to watch the European Cup final live on a giant video screen.
City officials estimated 30,000 people had crammed into Dortmund's Friedensplatz square before the kick-off to enjoy a pre-match programme of music and entertainment.
Fans wandered around fairground stalls throughout the city centre selling everything from chocolate hearts declaring affection for Borussia to inflatable European Cups.

A spokesman for the city council, Carsten Hensel, said he expected around 100,000 people to be somewhere in the centre to enjoy the match and was optimistic the fans would remain peaceful even if their team lost the Munich final.
"We'll wait and see but we've been doing these sorts of parties for years and we've always managed to conclude them successfully," he said.

Few Dortmund fans were willing to even contemplate the prospect that Borussia would not claim their first European trophy since 1966. Several wore T-shirts proclaiming Dortmund as "Champions' League winners 1996/97".
"I got this made for me today," said Dortmund resident Udo Grubinski, explaining there was space on the back of the shirt for the scoreline to be added later.
Kerstin Deutschmann, describing herself as a "housewife and full-time Borussia fan", proudly displayed her T-shirt featuring a photograph of her with Dortmund striker Stephane Chapuisat.
"He'll score at least one tonight," she predicted confidently.
The caterers and stallholders scattered around the square entered into the mood of the big occasion, many wearing Dortmund scarves. One was even selling special "champions' sausages".
"I hope to sell 1,000 of these tonight," said Hans-Joachim Wiechmann. "But it gets so packed here you can't sell too many."

One souvenir seller, who reported that a scarf bearing the shields of both Juventus and Dortmund was his best-selling item, found himself in a slightly awkward situation -- as an Italian from Turin surrounded by thousands of fanatical Dortmund supporters.
Asked who he wanted to win the match, Vladimiro Dimuro replied: "I'll say this very quietly -- Juventus".
